title: Sanremo: at the 42nd edition of the Italian Song Festival Luca Barbarossa wins with Portami a ballare.
text: Portami a ballare is a 1992 Italian song written and performed by singer-songwriter Luca Barbarossa.

title: the Catholic Church rehabilitates the Italian scientist Galileo Galilei, convicted in 1633.
text: Galileo di Vincenzo Bonaiuti de' Galilei, commonly referred to as Galileo Galilei or mononymously as Galileo, was an Italian astronomer, physicist, engineer and polymath. He was born in Pisa, then part of the Duchy of Florence.

title: “Black or White” by Michael Jackson
text: "Black or White" is a song by American singer and songwriter Michael Jackson, released by Epic Records on November 4, 1991, as the lead single from Jackson's eighth album, Dangerous. Jackson wrote, composed, and produced the track with record producer Bill Bottrell, who provides an uncredited rap performance.

title: “Mysterious Ways” by U2
text: "Mysterious Ways" is a song by Irish rock band U2. It is the eighth track from their seventh album, Achtung Baby, and was released as the album's second single on 2 December 1991 by Island Records, two weeks after the album.

title: “Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me” by George Michael and Elton John
text: "Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me" is a song by British musician Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin. It was originally recorded by John for his eighth studio album, Caribou, and was released as a single that peaked at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart, and reached number 16 on the UK Singles Chart.

listen: Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me George Michael and Elton John

title: “Human Touch” by Bruce Springsteen
text: "Human Touch" is a song recorded by the American rock singer and songwriter Bruce Springsteen. It was the first single from his tenth studio album of the same name and was released on March 9, 1992 by Columbia Records.

title: “Why” by Annie Lennox
text: "Why" is the debut solo single from Scottish singer-songwriter Annie Lennox, released on 16 March 1992 by RCA Records as the lead single from her debut solo album Diva. Written by Lennox and produced by Stephen Lipson, it has since become considered as a signature song for Lennox, and has been credited for its emotional songwriting technique.

title: “Rhythm Is a Dancer” by Snap!
text: "Rhythm Is a Dancer" is a song by German Eurodance group Snap!, released in March 1992 by Arista and Logic Records as the second single from their second studio album, The Madman's Return. It features vocals by American singer Thea Austin.

title: “Hanno ucciso l'Uomo Ragno” by 883
text: "Hanno ucciso l'Uomo Ragno" is a song by Italian pop group 883, released in 1992 as a single from their debut studio album of the same name. The song uses the Marvel Comics superhero Spider-Man as a symbol of lost ideals and the disillusionment of youth, while also reflecting on consumerism and the contradictions of modern society.

title: “This Used to Be My Playground” by Madonna
text: "This Used to Be My Playground" is a song recorded by American singer Madonna. It is the theme for the film A League of Their Own, in which Madonna appeared.

title: “Erotica” by Madonna
text: "Erotica" is a song by American singer Madonna from her fifth studio album of the same name. Madonna and Pettibone produced the song; they wrote it with Anthony Shimkin.

title: “Don't You Want Me” by Felix
text: "Don't You Want Me" is a song recorded by British DJ and producer Francis Wright, known under the pseudonym of Felix, released in July 1992 as his debut single from his album, #1. Musically, it samples Jomanda's "Don't You Want My Love" and credited as Felix featuring Jomanda (remixed by Rollo and Red Jerry).

title: “Deeper and Deeper” by Madonna
text: "Deeper and Deeper" is a song by American singer Madonna from her fifth studio album, Erotica. It was written by Madonna, Shep Pettibone, and Anthony Shimkin and was produced by Madonna and Pettibone.

title: Asteroid 5751 Zao is discovered by Masahiro Koishikawa.
text: An asteroid is a minor planet that orbits within the inner Solar System or is co-orbital with a planet. These objects are larger than a meteoroid (thus 1 meter or larger) and are neither a planet nor an identified comet.

title: First confirmed detection of exoplanets with announcement of the discovery of several terrestrial-mass planets orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12 by radio astronomers Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail working in the United States.
text: An exoplanet or extrasolar planet is a planet outside the Solar System. The first confirmed detection of an exoplanet was in 1992 around a pulsar, and the first detection around a main-sequence star was in 1995.

title: Discovery of 15760 Albion, the first trans-Neptunian object to be found after Pluto and Charon.
text: 15760 Albion is the first trans-Neptunian object discovered after Pluto and Charon. Measuring about 108–167 kilometres in diameter, it was discovered in 1992 by David C. Jewitt and Jane X. Luu at the Mauna Kea Observatory, Hawaii.

title: Pope John Paul II issues an apology and lifts the 1633 edict of the Inquisition against Galileo Galilei.
text: Pope John Paul II was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 16 October 1978 until his death in 2005. He was the first non-Italian pope since Adrian VI in the 16th century, as well as the third longest-serving pope in history, after St.

title: The Goosebumps series of children's horror fiction, penned by R. L. Stine, is first published in the United States.
text: Robert Lawrence Stine is an American novelist. He is the writer of Goosebumps, a horror fiction novel series for children which has sold over 400 million copies globally in 35 languages, becoming the second-best-selling book series in history.

title: An attempt is made to set fire to the National Library of Abkhazia in Sukhumi during the War in Abkhazia by Georgian forces.
text: The War in Abkhazia was fought between Georgian government and paramilitary forces, and a coalition of Abkhaz separatist forces and North Caucasian militants between 1992 and 1993. Ethnic Georgians who lived in Abkhazia fought largely on the side of Georgian government forces.

title: The National and University Library of Bosnia and Herzegovina is annihilated during the Siege of Sarajevo by the Army of Republika Srpska.
text: The Siege of Sarajevo was a prolonged military blockade of Sarajevo, the capital of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, during the Bosnian War. Beginning on 5 April 1992, the capital was surrounded by Bosnian Serb forces following the outbreak of the Bosnian War.

title: Michael Ondaatje's historiographic metafiction The English Patient is published in Canada. It will win The Golden Man Booker in 2018.
text: Philip Michael Ondaatje is a Sri Lankan-born Canadian poet, fiction writer and essayist. Ondaatje's literary career began with his poetry: in 1967 he published The Dainty Monsters, and in 1970 the critically acclaimed The Collected Works of Billy the Kid.

title: British fashion designer Alexander McQueen shows his first collection, partly inspired by The Silence of the Lambs (film).
text: Lee Alexander McQueen was a British fashion designer and couturier. Known for his unconventional designs, he was one of the most influential fashion designers in the world from the early 1990s until his death by suicide in 2010.

title: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum in Madrid is opened to the public as a gallery for the private art collection of the Thyssen-Bornemisza family.
text: The Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum, or simply the Thyssen, is an art museum in Madrid, Spain, located near the Prado Museum on one of the city's main boulevards. It is known as part of the "Golden Triangle of Art", which also includes the Prado and the Reina Sofía national galleries.
